title: Composite point-section pullback comparison: tower equation and actual common-stage actions
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, and an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$. All coefficient fields below are finite intermediate extensions of $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$, with valuation rings and uniformizers [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, and let $g:s\to s$ be a scheme automorphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], put $\mathcal C_E^{\rm int}=D^b_c(s,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], $\mathcal C_E=D^b_c(s,E)$, the raw rationalization [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], and $P_E=Lg_E^*$ with its specified integral, rational and common-stage actions [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Let $F_E^{\rm int}=\Gamma(s,-)$ and $F_E=\operatorname{Fib}_s:\mathcal C_E\to D^b_{\rm fd}(E)$ be the specified point-section functors [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], and put $H_E=F_EP_E$.

For $E\subseteq L$, write $S_{L/E}K=K\otimes_E L$ for rational scalar extension and $T_{L/E}A=A\otimes_E L$ on point complexes [def-weil-point-fd-qlbar-category]. Let $\bar\alpha_{E,L,K}:S_{L/E}P_EK\xrightarrow{\sim}P_LS_{L/E}K$ and $\bar\varphi_{E,L,K}:F_LS_{L/E}K\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{L/E}F_EK$ be precisely the rationalizations of the specified completed pullback and sections comparisons [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension, lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension]. Define
$$b_{E,L,K}=\bar\varphi_{E,L,P_EK}\circ F_L(\bar\alpha_{E,L,K}^{-1}):H_LS_{L/E}K\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{L/E}H_EK.$$

Write $a^C_{N,L,E}:S_{N/L}S_{L/E}\xrightarrow{\sim}S_{N/E}$ for the specified scalar associator [lem-weil-scalar-extension-composition], and $a^D_{N,L,E}:T_{N/L}T_{L/E}\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{N/E}$ for the point-complex associator [def-weil-point-fd-qlbar-category]. The maps $b$ are natural in every rational arrow of $\mathcal C_E$, are identities for $E=L$ under the unit identifications, and obey
$$b_{E,N,K}\circ H_N(a^C_{N,L,E,K})=a^D_{N,L,E,H_EK}\circ T_{N/L}(b_{E,L,K})\circ b_{L,N,S_{L/E}K}.$$

On the literal common-stage source $D^b_c(s,\Omega)$ [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] and target $D^b_{\rm fd}(\Omega)$ [def-weil-point-fd-qlbar-category], let $u:S_{L/E}K\to S_{L/E'}K'$ represent a morphism. The specified functors $\operatorname{Fib}_s$ and $\operatorname{Fib}_s\circ Lg^*$ send it to classes represented over the same $L$ by, respectively,
$$A_L(u)=\bar\varphi_{E',L,K'}F_L(u)\bar\varphi_{E,L,K}^{-1},\qquad B_L(u)=b_{E',L,K'}H_L(u)b_{E,L,K}^{-1}.$$
In particular $B_L(u)$ is the point-fiber image of the prescribed pullback representative $\bar\alpha_{E',L,K'}^{-1}P_L(u)\bar\alpha_{E,L,K}$. Both formulas preserve identity arrows and compositions at a common stage. If $N\supseteq L$, scalar extension of $A_L(u)$ and $B_L(u)$, conjugated by the specified point-complex associators, equals $A_N(u_N)$ and $B_N(u_N)$, where $u_N$ is source scalar transport using $a^C$. Thus the two functor actions have the same classes for every equivalent common-stage representative, without assuming injective transition maps. No family of transformation components is an input to these assertions.

For the literal Lean realization use the canonical small coefficient model $\operatorname{Shrink}(E)$ and the inclusions conjugated by its specified algebra equivalence with $E$, as in [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. All finite-field families and comparison equations use these same models; the common-stage target retains the prescribed transports back to the actual subfields. The duplicated rational and common-stage helper definitions are aliases of the canonical constructions in [lem-weil-point-rational-family-common-stage-naturality]; this concerns only its definitions, not that theorem as a proof assumption.

The completed pro-etale normalization and explicit formulas are an agent-written argument, not assertions attributed to Deligne.

proof.text: Rationalize the specified integral comparisons. The pullback comparison of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension] is natural, unital and compatible with successive coefficient extension; the sections comparison of [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension] has the displayed sections-tensor normalization, unit and tower equations, including after tensoring with the coefficient field. These apply at $s$ since $\ell\ne p$ and to $P_EK$ since the specified pullback is a functor on the integral constructible category. In the raw rationalization [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] every arrow is a finite sum $\sum_jv_j\otimes c_j$. The specified actions of $P_E$ [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and $F_E$ [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] send each summand to the image of $v_j$ multiplied by $c_j$. Thus each rational naturality square is the sum of $c_j$ times its integral naturality square, after embedding $E$ in the larger field. Tensoring the integral inverse identities, unit equations and tower equations gives those equations for exactly $\bar\alpha$ and $\bar\varphi$ in the statement. This verifies naturality on all rational arrows, not just arrows admitting an integral lift.

proof.text:
Put $d_{E,L,K}=\bar\alpha_{E,L,K}^{-1}$ and $\phi_{E,L,K}=\bar\varphi_{E,L,K}$. For a rational arrow $v:K\to K'$, naturality from step 1 gives
$$d_{E,L,K'}P_L(S_{L/E}v)=S_{L/E}(P_Ev)d_{E,L,K},\qquad \phi_{E,L,P_EK'}F_L(S_{L/E}P_Ev)=T_{L/E}(H_Ev)\phi_{E,L,P_EK}.$$
Apply $F_L$ to the first equality and substitute in the second. The result is $b_{E,L,K'}H_L(S_{L/E}v)=T_{L/E}(H_Ev)b_{E,L,K}$, since $b=\phi F_L(d)$. Every factor is an isomorphism; when $L=E$ both factors are identities under the specified units, by the unit clauses of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension, lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension].

proof.text:
Fix $E\subseteq L\subseteq N$. For this calculation abbreviate $S=S_{L/E}$, $U=S_{N/L}$, $T=T_{L/E}$, $V=T_{N/L}$, $a=a^C_{N,L,E}$ and $c=a^D_{N,L,E}$. The pullback tower equation of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension], inverted, reads
$$d_{E,N,K}P_N(a_K)=a_{P_EK}\,U(d_{E,L,K})\,d_{L,N,SK}.$$
Its associator is the scalar associator specified by [lem-weil-scalar-extension-composition]. The sections tower equation of [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension] reads
$$\phi_{E,N,J}F_N(a_J)=c_{F_EJ}\,V(\phi_{E,L,J})\,\phi_{L,N,SJ}.$$
These are equations of rational derived morphisms by step 1. We will use them with $J=P_EK$; all objects remain in the stated coefficient categories.

proof.text:
Expand the right side of the required $b$ equation using the notation of step 3:
$$c_{H_EK}V(b_{E,L,K})b_{L,N,SK}
=c_{H_EK}V(\phi_{E,L,P_EK})V(F_Ld_{E,L,K})\phi_{L,N,P_LSK}F_N(d_{L,N,SK}).$$
Naturality of $\phi_{L,N}$, supplied by [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension] and rationalized in step 1, at the arrow $d_{E,L,K}:P_LSK\to SP_EK$ replaces the middle pair $V(F_Ld)\phi_{L,N,P_LSK}$ by $\phi_{L,N,SP_EK}F_N(Ud)$. The sections tower equation of step 3 now changes the first three factors to $\phi_{E,N,P_EK}F_N(a_{P_EK})$. Hence the whole product is
$$\phi_{E,N,P_EK}F_N(a_{P_EK}U(d_{E,L,K})d_{L,N,SK})
=\phi_{E,N,P_EK}F_N(d_{E,N,K}P_N(a_K))
=b_{E,N,K}H_N(a_K),$$
by the pullback equation of step 3 and functoriality. This is the asserted tower equation, with both associators in their displayed directions.

proof.text:
For $u: S_{L/E}K\to S_{L/E'}K'$, the actual point functor sends $[L,u]$ to $[L,A_L(u)]$ by clause 4 of [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. The prescribed pullback action in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] represents $Lg^*[L,u]$ by
$$v=d_{E',L,K'}P_L(u)\bar\alpha_{E,L,K}:S_{L/E}P_EK\to S_{L/E'}P_{E'}K'.$$
Apply clause 4 of the point functor to this very representative, with objects $P_EK,P_{E'}K'$. Its representative is
$$\phi_{E',L,P_{E'}K'}F_L(v)\phi_{E,L,P_EK}^{-1}
=(\phi'F_L(d'))H_L(u)(F_L(\bar\alpha)\phi^{-1})
=b_{E',L,K'}H_L(u)b_{E,L,K}^{-1}.$$
Thus the second formula computes the specified composite functor, rather than merely defining another candidate action.

proof.text:
At a fixed common field $L$, write either formula from step 5 as $X_L(u)=D_{K'}G_L(u)D_K^{-1}$: take $(G,D)=(F,\phi)$ for $A$ and $(G,D)=(H,b)$ for $B$. Then
$$X_L(1)=D_K1D_K^{-1}=1,\qquad X_L(v)X_L(u)=D_{K''}G_L(v)(D_{K'}^{-1}D_{K'})G_L(u)D_K^{-1}=X_L(vu).$$
This uses only functoriality and inverse cancellation. The common-stage composition and unit conventions of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients, def-weil-point-fd-qlbar-category] are exactly these operations after passing to classes; at a field equal to an endpoint, the specified units give the same identities.

proof.text:
Check further extension explicitly. Keep either choice $(G,D)$ of step 6 and put $U=S_{N/L}$, $V=T_{N/L}$, $a_K=a^C_{N,L,E,K}$ and $c_K=a^D_{N,L,E,G_EK}$, with primes for $(E',K')$. The tower equation is
$$D_{E,N,K}G_N(a_K)=c_K V(D_{E,L,K})D_{L,N,S_{L/E}K}.$$
For $D=\phi$ this is [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension]; for $D=b$ it is step 4. The source transition is $u_N=a_{K'}U(u)a_K^{-1}$ [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Substituting these three equations in $X_N(u_N)$ gives
$$c_{K'}V(D_{E',L,K'})D_{L,N,S_{L/E'}K'}G_N(Uu)D_{L,N,S_{L/E}K}^{-1}V(D_{E,L,K}^{-1})c_K^{-1}.$$
Naturality of $D_{L,N}$ at the rational arrow $u$ replaces the middle three factors by $V(G_Lu)$, so this equals
$$c_{K'}V\bigl(D_{E',L,K'}G_L(u)D_{E,L,K}^{-1}\bigr)c_K^{-1}=c_{K'}V(X_L(u))c_K^{-1}.$$
This is precisely the point-complex transition formula of [def-weil-point-fd-qlbar-category]. Naturality needed here is step 1 for $\phi$ and step 2 for $b$, and applies even when $u$ is an arbitrary sum of rational tensors.

proof.text: If $[L,u]=[L',v]$ in the literal source, [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] says $u_N=v_N$ at some finite common extension $N\supseteq L,L'$. Step 7 identifies the target transitions of $A_L(u),A_{L'}(v)$ with $A_N(u_N),A_N(v_N)$, which are equal; the identical argument using $B_N$ treats $B$. By the target equality criterion in [def-weil-point-fd-qlbar-category] their classes therefore agree. Together with step 6 this proves independence of representatives and of the field used for composition. Only equality at a later stage was used, so no injectivity of any transition is required. Every construction in steps 1-8 uses only the fixed functors and their scalar comparisons; no transformation component or family of such components was supplied.

In particular $B_L(u)$ is the point-fiber image of the prescribed pullback representative $\bar\alpha_{E',L,K'}^{-1}P_L(u)\bar\alpha_{E,L,K}$. Both formulas preserve identity arrows and compositions at a common stage. If $N\supseteq L$, scalar extension of $A_L(u)$ and $B_L(u)$, conjugated by the specified point-complex associators, equals $A_N(u_N)$ and $B_N(u_N)$, where $u_N$ is source scalar transport using $a^C$. Thus the two functor actions have the same classes for every equivalent common-stage representative, without assuming injective transition maps. No family of transformation components is an input to these assertions.
